modelIntro.title: Create AI Videos Directly From Text
description: Toolaze Text to Video Generator focuses on prompt-first video creation for short clips, social ads, product motion, storyboards, explainers, and B-roll ideas. Use it when the scene can be described in words and you do not need to upload a reference image.

Start with a compact prompt, structured script, or product brief, then choose a supported video model and output settings. Credit requirements are shown before generation and vary by selected model, duration, resolution, audio options, and quality settings.

troubleshooting.title: How to Improve Text to Video Results
troubleshooting.subtitle: Write one clear action, one camera direction, and one visual style before adding more detail.

items.title: Motion is too busy
items.desc: Keep one subject action and one camera movement. Too many competing movements make short clips unstable.
items.prompt: Try: A single product rotates slowly while the camera makes one gentle push-in.

items.title: Scene lacks direction
items.desc: Add shot order, lighting, time of day, camera lens, and ending frame so the model has a clearer target.
items.prompt: Try: Start wide, move to a close-up, end on the product label.

items.title: Credits are too high
items.desc: Test shorter duration or lower resolution before using more credits on the final direction.
items.prompt: Try a 5-second draft, then increase settings after the motion works.

promptExamples.subtitle: Copy these prompt patterns to test scripts, social hooks, camera movement, pacing, format, and model fit.

items.title: Editorial portrait shot prompt
items.prompt: Create a 5-second widescreen editorial portrait video of a young creative professional standing near a large studio window. Use a slow push-in camera, a gentle head turn, subtle hair and fabric movement, soft natural light, shallow depth of field, realistic skin texture, calm confident mood, and a clean neutral background. No logos, no celebrity likeness.
items.description: Widescreen Grok text-to-video portrait example with soft window light, subtle motion, and a slow push-in camera.
items.note: Use this for portrait clips where the subject, light, and camera movement need to be easy to describe.

items.title: Renewable explainer B-roll prompt
items.prompt: Create a 5-second explainer B-roll clip for a lesson about renewable energy. Show sunlight moving across rooftop solar panels, a close-up of an energy meter rising, and a clean classroom-style graphic transition. Calm motion, realistic daylight, gentle camera pan, educational presentation tone.
items.description: Widescreen Grok text-to-video example for educational renewable energy B-roll.
items.note: Use this for lessons, explainers, and presentation clips that need neutral supporting footage.

items.title: Bridge tracking shot prompt
items.prompt: Create a 5-second widescreen cinematic shot of a cyclist crossing a quiet bridge at sunset. Use one smooth left-to-right tracking move, warm backlight, shallow depth of field, realistic motion blur, and a final frame where the cyclist exits into the glow.
items.description: Widescreen Grok text-to-video example testing one cyclist action and one smooth tracking shot.
items.note: Use this to test one subject action and one camera move before adding more detail.

items.title: Travel product concept prompt
items.prompt: Create a 5-second product concept video for a compact travel coffee grinder. Show the grinder on a hotel desk, beans pouring into the top, a quick close-up of the dial, and a final frame with a clean cup beside a city window. Soft morning light, premium travel gear mood, steady push-in camera.
items.description: Widescreen Grok text-to-video example for a fictional compact travel coffee grinder concept.
items.note: Use this when a product idea needs a quick visual concept before a shoot.

faq.q: What is a text to video generator?
faq.a: A text to video generator turns a written prompt into a short video clip. On Toolaze, you describe the scene, action, camera movement, and style, then choose a supported AI video model.

faq.q: Is text to video free on Toolaze?
faq.a: Toolaze may provide free credits or selected trial access, but video generation credit requirements depend on the selected model and settings. The generation flow shows the required credits before you start.

faq.q: How long can text-to-video clips be?
faq.a: Typical text-to-video clips on Toolaze are short-form outputs, often between 3 and 15 seconds depending on the selected model and settings. Use shorter drafts to test motion, camera direction, and prompt wording before increasing duration or quality.

faq.q: Does text to video include audio or subtitles?
faq.a: Audio, voice, and subtitle support depends on the selected video model and available settings. If the selected model does not provide native audio or captions, generate the visual clip first and add subtitles, voiceover, or music in an editor.

faq.q: What can I create with text to video?
faq.a: Use text to video for social hooks, product ads, B-roll, storyboards, explainers, concept clips, and camera-movement tests. It works best when the scene can be described clearly without relying on a specific uploaded reference image.

faq.q: What is the difference between text-to-video and image-to-video?
faq.a: Text-to-video starts from a written scene description and gives the model more freedom to invent the look. Image-to-video starts from a reference image, which helps preserve a product, character, layout, composition, or visual style while adding motion.

faq.q: What should I write in a text to video prompt?
faq.a: Include the subject, action, camera movement, lighting, mood, pacing, aspect ratio, and final frame. Keep the first draft simple, then add detail after the motion works.

faq.q: Can I use generated text-to-video clips commercially?
faq.a: Commercial use depends on the selected model, Toolaze account status, source materials, and applicable terms. Avoid using restricted brands, people, or copyrighted assets without rights, and review the latest usage rules before publishing client or paid work.
